title: Step 34: Mode-diagonal indicial structure and resonance on flat A₁ cone
scope: Route A noncollapsed positive subroute; not a proof of Yau-26.

mode_diagonality.statement: On flat R⁴/{±1}, the bilinear form Ric_e^{(2)}(h,k)(X,∂_r) preserves angular degree l. Cross-mode pairs l ≠ l' integrate to zero by orthogonality of tensor harmonics on S³/Z₂.
mode_diagonality.source: Ozuch 2021 line 626: Ric_e^{(2)} maps l=2 to l=2
mode_diagonality.consequence: The Wronskian/Taub obstruction integral pairs only within the same angular mode. This is WHY α + β = -2 (same l on both sides).

pairing_table.balance_radius: r = t^(2/3) (our convention: t⁴ ALE coefficient)

entries.label: l=0 (mass/volume)
entries.gauge_status: pure gauge on growing side; mass/volume on decaying side
entries.note: Larger than l=2 modes in absolute size, but invisible by mode-diagonality

entries.label: l=2 (H₂/H⁴ Ozuch obstruction)
entries.gauge_status: first non-gauge mode; signal = R⁺·v (Ozuch Cor 4.10)
entries.note: This IS the obstruction. Nonzero iff det R_+ ≠ 0.

entries.label: l=4 (higher curvature)
entries.note: Angular-orthogonal to l=2 test; contributes at higher order

cross_modes_all_zero.reason: angular orthogonality: ∫ T_2 · T_0 = 0 on S³/Z₂
angular orthogonality: ∫ T_2 · T_4 = 0 on S³/Z₂
angular orthogonality: ∫ T_0 · T_2 = 0 on S³/Z₂
angular orthogonality: ∫ T_4 · T_2 = 0 on S³/Z₂

same_direction_all_zero.note: Wronskian of a mode with itself vanishes: W[f,f]=0

same_direction_all_zero.size_at_balance: would give t⁴ × t⁴ / t^(16/3) = t^(8/3)
same_direction_all_zero.note: Antisymmetry: W[f,f]=0; also angular: Ric^{(2)}(H⁴,H⁴) is O(r⁻⁸), subleading

pairing_table.conclusion: At the balance radius, the ONLY flux-visible contribution at O(t⁴) is the l=2 dual pair (H₂, t⁴H⁴). The l=0 mass mode is larger in absolute size (O(t^{2/3}) > O(t^{4/3})) but angular-orthogonal. Higher modes are subleading. Same-direction pairings vanish.

resonance.resonance_type: logarithmic (rate r⁰ source resonates with r² homogeneous mode)

balance_evaluation.consequence: If δ and t go to zero independently, the resonance gives relative error δ log(1/t), which is NOT automatically small. The A2 bridge carries the hypothesis δ log(1/t) → 0 UNLESS the Bianchi constraint removes the resonant l=2 source component.

bianchi_constraint.question: Does the divergence-free constraint on the l=2 projection of E remove the constant (r⁰) radial component, thereby killing the logarithmic resonance?
bianchi_constraint.preliminary_analysis: For a TT tensor T₂ of degree 2 on S³, div_e(S(r)T₂) = 0 on R⁴ imposes S' + (3/r)S - c/r S = 0 for some constant c depending on the tensor type. If c = 3, solution is S = const (resonance survives). If c ≠ 3, S ~ r^{c-3} and the constant source is killed.
bianchi_constraint.load_bearing_status: If Bianchi removes the resonance: A2 bridge is rate-free (relative error O(δ), no log correction). If not: A2 carries the additional hypothesis δ_i log(1/t_i) → 0, which is a rate condition on the pinching-to-bubble-scale coupling.
bianchi_constraint.next_computation: Explicit divergence of S(r) × (θ_l⁻ ∘ ω_k⁺) on R⁴ in polar coordinates, to determine the exact constraint on S(r).

bianchi_refinement.critical_point: The Bianchi constraint div_g E = 0 applies to the TOTAL error, not to each l-component separately. The l=2 projection of E need not itself be divergence-free. Therefore the resonance CANNOT be removed by the Bianchi identity alone.
bianchi_refinement.rate_hypothesis: Route A therefore carries the hypothesis δ_i log(1/t_i) → 0. In many geometric sequences, t ~ δ^{α} for some α > 0, so log(1/t) ~ α log(1/δ) and δ log(1/t) ~ αδ log(1/δ) → 0. But an a priori statement needs either a rate relation or a structural improvement (e.g., L²-projection killing the resonant source).
bianchi_refinement.alternative_escape: If the noncollapsed sequence has a uniform harmonic-radius lower bound at scale r, then the metric in harmonic coordinates has C^{1,α} control, and the l=2 source projection has improved regularity that may kill the resonance. This connects the resonance question to the harmonic-radius epsilon lemma.

route_A_update.mode_diagonality: CONFIRMED: Wronskian is l-diagonal, l=0 invisible, l=2 IS obstruction
route_A_update.gauge_triviality_l0: CONFIRMED: l=0 growing mode is pure gauge, l=0 decaying is mass
route_A_update.resonance_severity: MODERATE: δ log(1/t) rate condition, not δ × (power of t)
resolution_paths: 1. Accept δ log(1/t) → 0 as a mild additional hypothesis (covers most geometric sequences)
2. Prove harmonic-radius epsilon lemma → improved l=2 source regularity → resonance killed
3. Show that in the specific EH/orbifold geometry, the l=2 Bianchi constraint IS exact
route_A_update.A2_bridge_precise_statement: At r ≈ t^{2/3}, the metric equals e + A₂ r² T₂ + t⁴ B₋₄ r⁻⁴ T₂ + (l=0 mass/gauge) + (l≥4 subleading) + corrections. The l=2 Wronskian signal is t⁴ R⁺·v. The relative error is O(δ) + O(δ log(1/t)). If δ log(1/t) → 0, nonzero R⁺·v forces δ bounded away from zero.
